decisions.D5-1 the regimes (owner's brief): on every decode tile the CORES rho tail is removed (the GEMM at bandwidth, its partial wave at its compute floor) and gemm = max(G_bw s, b / r_cta,t) + d b / r1_t, d = 1 when n > S, at DS's SUBWAVE r_cta,t and DRAIN r1_t (DS's registered fits, unchanged). Alternative tried: SUBWAVE re-read on DS's own ladders with one offset per (tile, GEMM) instead of one per ladder (r_cta 49.7, 27.5, 27.5, 56.0 GB/s; its rms on DS's rows 7 to 10% against the registered fit's 2 to 5%); CAL2 reads the same STOP (worst cell -10.67%). Not taken
decisions.D5-2 the paths: SUBWAVE, DRAIN and W1 act on the aligned paths only (small-batch, block-scan); the naive path keeps v4d''s GEMM price. Why: DS read no naive row (its GEMM readings take small-batch and block-scan cells only), and a naive GEMM's CTAs are not one slab each (a repeated expert's slab is served from L2). Alternative: every path (the first build): CAL2 rms 2.60% against 2.41%, both STOP on the same cell. Chosen on CAL2 and DS's row set. FORKING PATH, disclosed: the every-path variant had already been re-scored on the SEEN blind (3.52% pooled) before this choice; the choice was made on CAL2 alone and goes against that re-score (v5d reads 4.41%)
decisions.D5-3 W1: s_t = 3577.96 / c_t (DS's W1RATE) on the three larger tiles scales w1's bandwidth part only (DS read b / r_cta and b / r1 in counter time); fix R stays on 16x64x128w4s4 (DS re-read it at 0.917911 against 0.918488, a replicate). Alternatives: s_t on the whole w1 price, ceiling and drain included: CAL2 2.41%, worst -10.78%; w2 also at the counters' 3895.49 GB/s (DS assumed that rate for w2 and did not measure it): CAL2 3.28%, worst -12.44%. Not taken
decisions.D5-4 CALL: B_other (the call kernels' bytes at DRAM speed) is replaced by silu_and_mul a + g B / 1 MB and moe_sum a + h k + g B / 1 MB, the coefficients by OLS on DS's NATIVE rows (69 per class, six models). The forms were chosen by leave-one-model-out rms on DS's six models (DS pages only; 16 candidates compared, 15 distinct as [1, T k I] duplicates [1, B]; a forking path on DS's pages): silu_and_mul [1, B] 0.529 us (against [1] 1.633, [1, I] 1.418, [1, I, B] 0.808 (the DS summary line), [1, T k] 1.674, [1, I, T k] 1.101); moe_sum [1, k, B] 0.201 us (against [1] 0.817, [1, B] 0.704, [1, k H] 0.541, [1, k H, B] 0.509 (the DS summary line), [1, k] 0.387, [1, H, k] 0.437, [1, k, T H] 0.262, [1, k H, T H] 0.570). CAL2 with the DS summary-line forms: 2.36%, the same STOP. k: DS spans 2, 4 and 8, the new models' 2 and 8; B: Mixtral-8x22B's largest silu_and_mul B is 1.14 x DS's largest and Qwen2-57B's largest moe_sum B 1.75 x, both extrapolated along the fitted line
decisions.D5-5 ALIGN: DS's align points (small-batch at one loop iteration; block-scan, BLOCK) piecewise linear in E between the measured E and held at the nearest measured E outside them (never extrapolated), 0 on the naive path; plus SLOPE 0.526921 us x (iterations - 1) on the small-batch path. The new models' E: Mixtral-8x22B E 8 and Qwen2-57B E 64 are measured points (Qwen2-57B's block-scan at E 64 measured too); Granite-1B's small-batch E 32 is the DECL point (DECL TRANSFERS) and its block-scan E 32 is NOT measured: held at E 40's 8.704 us (linear extrapolation from E 40 and 64 would read 8.896 us). Alternatives: SLOPE's per-E intercepts in place of the one-iteration medians: CAL2 2.40%; no slope: 2.54%, worst -11.32%
decisions.D5-6 the CAL constants: T0_GR, s_naive and s_block refitted on CAL2's kept cells under v5d (v4d's registered fit and rho selection, score_cal_d3's rules); nothing else is fitted on CAL2
decisions.D5-7 the three weak DS readings (coordin: kept at DS's constants: no refit, no fallback, no term dropped (dropping one would be a further choice, and CAL2 prefers none of the drops: no drain on 32x64x128w4s3 2.45%, W1 off on 32x128x64w4s3 2.47%, against 2.41%). How far each transfers to the new models, from their configs and registered page lists only (prices at the CAL2 refit's constants, no page of theirs): (1) SUBWAVE: r_cta binds on one JetMoE w2 row per tile (n 64, 128, 96, 64), so it is a one-model reading; under v5d it binds on 0 of the 143 new main cells and 0 of CAL2's 91 (the new models' single-wave GEMMs hold 128 to 512 CTAs, none for Qwen2-57B, against JetMoE's binding rows of 64 to 128; b / r_cta is at most 0.63 of the GEMM at bandwidth on Granite-1B, 0.40 on Mixtral-8x22B and 0.17 on Qwen2-57B, so r_cta would have to read 1.6, 2.5 and 5.9 times lower to bind), so the new predictions do not depend on it; with no ceiling anywhere every new prediction is unchanged. (2) W1RATE on 32x128x64w4s3 (2 ladders, SE 49 GB/s): c moved by one SE moves 5 cells per model by at most 0.80% (Mixtral-8x22B), 0.78% (Qwen2-57B), 0.37% (Granite-1B); dropping the scale there moves them by at most 5.2%. (3) DRAIN on 32x64x128w4s3 (q 2.2 SE from 0, 5 crossing rows): it acts on 6 main cells each of Mixtral-8x22B and Qwen2-57B (none of Granite-1B); q set to 0 moves them by at most 5.9% and 6.0% (rms 1.4% per model), q + 2 SE by at most 5.3% and 5.4%. These 6 + 6 cells are where a weak DS reading can carry a new model's worst cell past 8% on its own; the blind scorer reports per cell, so a failure there is attributable to this reading

new blind design.scope line: Certified domain: decode calls in which every active expert fits in one M-tile (at most BLOCK_M rows). Calls where an expert needs a second M-tile (the most concentrated routing at T >= 32) are not certified; they are reported as the descriptive SIGMA-D row. Certification covers time as a function of the expert counts only: it does not cover a dependence on which experts are active (Mixtral's published expert-set effect, up to about 2.5 us at R 1). G3-D label, the test of that dependence, is DESCRIPTIVE (addendum 3, owner 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-03): it is reported per model and neither stops the CAL2 reading nor voids a blind model's certification; G3-D shuffle and GD2 void as registered.
